passage: Santosh sat under the neem tree behind the panchayat school, his hands shaking. He had just seen Hansa laughing with another boy outside the tea stall, just two weeks after she ended things. His face burned. He pulled out his phone and looked at the photo of the two of them at the fair. His thumb hovered. Post it with a nasty line? Send her one word that would sting? For a minute the anger felt like petrol. Then he threw the phone into his bag, took out his notebook, and wrote everything he wanted to say, pressing so hard the page tore. Then he ran three laps around the kabaddi ground until his lungs burned. Afterwards he sat by his friend Bhola and said, "I'm so angry I could scream." Bhola just said, "Okay. Tell me."

qa.q: Where was Santosh sitting when he saw Hansa?
qa.a: He was sitting under the neem tree behind the panchayat school.

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling when he looked at the photo?
qa.a: Furious and hurt. His face burned and the anger felt like petrol, tempting him to post it or send her something that would sting.

qa.q: What did Santosh do with his anger that was wise?
qa.a: He wrote it in his notebook, ran laps and told his friend Bhola, and did not post or send anything to Hansa.

qa.q: How might Hansa see the moment if Santosh had posted the photo?
qa.a: She would probably feel embarrassed and hurt, and unsafe with him. Keeping his anger private protected her and himself.

grounding: Santosh is furious at his ex and wants her to feel it, but writes it out, exercises, tells a friend and sends or posts nothing.

passage:
Afreen, you're angry at him. Good. Anger means you cared. But listen to what I did at your age.
When I was sixteen, in Kanpur, Shaheen broke up with me by a note in my geography book. Two days later she was laughing with another boy by the canteen. I was so furious I shook. I had photos of us, and her messages. I sat with my finger on the button, ready to send them to the whole class. I wanted her to feel what I felt.
The turning point was my cousin Irfan. He took the phone out of my hand and said, "If you send that, you become the story. Not her."
So instead I wrote five pages in a notebook, every angry word. Then I ran around the colony ground until I couldn't breathe. That night, I told Irfan everything, again and again.
I never sent anything. Your Naveen Chacha's proudest moment, that.

qa.q: How did Shaheen break up with young Naveen?
qa.a: By a note in his geography book.

qa.q: How did young Naveen feel when he saw Shaheen with another boy?
qa.a: He felt furious, shaking with anger and wanting her to feel as hurt as he did.

qa.q: What was the turning point, and what did Naveen do instead of sending the photos?
qa.a: His cousin Irfan took the phone away; Naveen then wrote out his anger, ran around the colony ground and talked to Irfan.

qa.q: How might Shaheen have been affected if the photos had been sent?
qa.a: She would have been humiliated in front of the whole class, and Naveen would have become the one who did something cruel.

grounding: An elder recalls his fury after a breakup and choosing to write, exercise and talk rather than share his ex's photos or messages.

passage:
It was board exam week, and Dilnaz still had to sit through tuition with Madhav, who'd broken up with her by text on Monday and then posted a photo with his new group on Wednesday, grinning.
She was so angry her pen tore the page. At home she opened their old chat. There was one photo of him in his school play costume, looking ridiculous. Posting it would take one second. He deserved it.
Her thumb hovered. Then she thought of how she'd feel if he did the same to her.
She shut the phone in her drawer, pulled out her rough notebook and wrote in big furious letters: I HATE THAT YOU MADE ME FEEL STUPID. She filled three pages.
Then she skipped rope on the terrace until her calves burned.
At night she called her friend Nargis and ranted for twenty minutes. Nargis just listened. The next morning, Dilnaz sat for her chemistry paper and didn't once look at his account.

qa.q: When did Madhav break up with Dilnaz?
What was Dilnaz feeling when she opened their old chat?
qa.a: She felt furious and humiliated, wanting Madhav to feel it by posting his embarrassing photo.

qa.q: Which choices kept Dilnaz from doing harm?
qa.a: She shut the phone away, wrote her anger in a notebook, skipped rope, and ranted to Nargis instead of posting anything.

qa.q: How might Madhav be affected if Dilnaz had posted the photo?
qa.a: He could have been embarrassed in front of everyone during exam week, and Dilnaz would have become the one causing harm.

grounding: A teen furious after a breakup writes it out, exercises and talks to a friend instead of posting her ex's photo.
